title: Console surge-mode MVP slice and graceful-fallback specification
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Context: The Console MVP needs a minimal set of dashboards, tracing, and per-route cost breakdowns but telemetry collection and dashboard rendering create high unit cost for the hosted offering. This ticket defines a narrowly scoped MVP slice and a 'surge-mode' graceful degradation strategy that reduces telemetry and UI surface area under load or when cost thresholds are approached. The goal is predictable latency, bounded cost, and clear acceptance criteria for launch.
scope_changes: Remove: real-time anomaly detection and automatic root-cause attribution from MVP (deferred to post-MVP).
Defer: long-tail storage of full trace spans beyond 7 days; retain sampled spans and aggregated metrics only for 30 days in MVP.
Trim: dashboard card templates limited to 6 highest-priority route cards instead of unlimited configurable cards.
Cut: interactive flamegraph UI; provide static trace summaries and latency histograms instead for initial release.
Include: per-route tokenized cost estimator card (approximate) with explicit confidence band; exact per-token accounting deferred.
decisions: Adopt 'surge-mode' flag that switches telemetry sampling to 1-5% and switches UI to low-bandwidth cards when monthly telemetry egress cost > configured threshold.
Prioritize latency SLO and first-byte response for Console over complete trace capture during surge-mode.
Expose 'surge-mode' state and basic explanation to customers in the UI and an API flag so platform teams can opt-out or increase quota.
Use existing metrics pipeline (ENG-1842) and add a light-weight serializer for sampled traces to minimize CPU overhead.
Roll out release behind feature flag with canary in two high-traffic orgs before wide release.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Console shows 6 configured route cards and associated latency and cost summary for each route in non-surge mode; cards render within 800ms on a 95th percentile client connection.

AC2: When monthly telemetry egress cost > $X (configurable), Console enters surge-mode: telemetry sampling reduces to <=5% and UI switches to lightweight summary cards; state is visible in the top banner.
AC3: Surge-mode toggles are surfaced via the admin API and documented in the PRD and runbook.

AC4: Traces captured in MVP include span-level timing and top 3 attributes; full span payloads are omitted in surge-mode; retention and sampling behavior match the spec and are validated by end-to-end test harness.

AC5: Cost delta estimate for enabling/disabling caching and batching suggestions is displayed on route cards with an estimated error bound; estimates exist for top 20 routes and match backend simulation within 25% error on synthetic workloads.
AC6: Feature-flagged canary rollout completes without regression to latency SLOs for 2 canary orgs over a 72-hour window; documented rollback plan exists and is rehearsed once.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal dogfooding + QA (2 weeks). Stage 2: canary enablement in 2 high-traffic customers with feature flag for 72h. Stage 3: open to all customers on alpha with opt-out API. Stage 4: post-alpha telemetry review and iterate on sampling thresholds. Rollback plan: immediate feature-flag disable and auto-rollback if latency SLO or error budgets exceeded by 3x during canary.
notes: Estimate X: This is a conservative points estimate reflecting backend changes to sampling and a trimmed UI surface implementation.
Tradeoff: Reducing sampling aggressively will impact fidelity of postmortems; the runbook requires increasing retention temporarily for customers under investigation.
PM asks: ENG to provide benchmark of CPU and egress delta for 1%, 5%, 10% sampling with current pipeline.
